transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it's nice to meet you too. Um... well, I guess I'm just here because I've been feeling a little bit off lately. It's probably nothing major, but my head just feels kind of... foggy, I suppose? I work as a personal care aide, and I've been making these silly little mistakes in my client notes, or I'll walk into a room and just sort of forget what I was about to do. It's really not like me at all, I'm usually very on top of things. I hope I'm explaining that okay? I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job at work, you know?
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Well... um, I don't want to sound dramatic or anything, because I really am trying to keep a positive attitude. But... I guess maybe a little bit? Lately, I've been waking up with this... this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. 

I mean, I still get through my shifts just fine, and I can talk to people and be cheerful for my clients, but... inside, I just feel kind of sad and flat. I hope it's okay to admit that? I just feel bad complaining when I'm supposed to be the one taking care of people. Does that make sense?
Have you been enjoying things less than you usually do?

Actually, um... no, I don't think so. I still really enjoy my usual hobbies and things. I like to work in my garden on the weekends, and that still feels just as nice as it always does. 

I try really hard to make sure I'm still doing things that make me smile, just so I don't let that... that heavy feeling take over completely. I hope that's a good sign? I mean, it's probably a good thing that I can still enjoy my time off, right?
How has your sleep been lately?

Well, um... my sleep hasn't been perfect, I suppose. It's probably just normal stress, though, you know? But, um, it has been a little all over the place lately. 

Sometimes I'll just lie there at night, and my mind will get a bit stuck thinking about family stuff, just worrying about everyone making sure they're okay. Or I'll wake up way before my alarm goes off, and I just can't seem to settle back down and get comfortable again. I mean, I still get enough rest to do my job, so it's not a huge problem or anything. I hope it's normal to have a few rough nights here and there? I'm sure everybody deals with that sometimes.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot lately?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I worry a *lot*. I mean, I care about my family and my clients, so of course I think about them and want to make sure everyone is doing okay. That's just part of who I am, I think. 

I try really hard not to let things get to me too much. Sometimes my mind might get a little busy, like I mentioned with the sleeping, but I don't think it's anything excessive. I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job and being there for the people who need me. That's a pretty normal amount of worrying, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm not making a big deal out of nothing.
Have these memory or concentration problems started to interfere with your work?

Well, um... I wouldn't say it's interfering, exactly. I mean, I'm still getting everything done, and my clients are all taken care of. I just... I want to make sure I'm doing things right, you know? 

So, um, I have been asking some of my coworkers to just double-check my documentation lately. Just to be safe, because I want to be thorough. And, well, at home, my wife has been helping out a little more with the bills and the scheduling. I just haven't felt quite as sharp with all those little details, so she offered to take over for a bit. It's really nice of her, and I think it's good to ask for help when you need it, right? I just want to make sure I'm not letting anything slip through the cracks. That's a responsible way to handle it, don't you think?
Did this foggy feeling start after something particularly stressful or upsetting happened in your life?

Well, um... I guess you could say that, yeah. It hasn't been going on forever or anything. Just, um... well, my uncle passed away about two weeks ago. 

It was a bit of a shock, and, you know, we were pretty close. So I think it's just natural to feel a little off after something like that, right? Anyone would be a bit distracted or foggy while they're processing a loss. I just... I really think it's just a normal reaction to grief, don't you? It's only been a couple of weeks, so I'm sure it'll pass once things settle down a bit.
Since your uncle died, have you been finding yourself longing for him or preoccupied with thoughts of him?

Well, um... no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, of course I miss him, because we were close, but I'm not... I'm not just sitting around dwelling on it all day or anything. 

I really try to keep my focus on my clients and my family. I'll think about the good memories we had sometimes, sure, but it's definitely not a preoccupation. I'm just trying to keep moving forward and handle it the best I can. That's the healthiest way to grieve, isn't it? I just wouldn't want you to think I'm falling apart or letting it take over my life. I think I'm managing it pretty normally, right?
Since your uncle died, have you felt sad or down for most of the day nearly every day?

Well, um... I guess I have been feeling a little down, yeah. But not, like, completely falling apart or anything! I mean, I still go to work, I still talk to everyone... I'm getting through my shifts just fine. 

It's just... lately, when I wake up, there's this sort of... heavy, empty feeling in my chest? Like, I can put on a smile for my clients, but inside I just feel kind of sad and... flat, I guess. But I think that's pretty normal when you're grieving, right? It's okay to feel a little sad for a while after losing someone, don't you think? I just wouldn't want you to worry that I'm not handling it well, because I really am trying my best to stay positive.
Have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

Oh, no, no, I would never... I mean, I don't have any plans to do anything like that. I really don't want you to think I'm, you know, a danger to myself or anything. I know how important it is to keep going for my family and my clients. 

But, um... I guess... well, there have been a couple of mornings lately where... where I just sort of think, maybe it wouldn't be the worst thing in the world if I just... didn't wake up? Just to not have to feel that heaviness for a bit. But it's just a fleeting thought, you know? It actually kind of scares me when it happens, because that's not who I am at all. I'm usually such a positive person. That's just the grief talking, right? It doesn't mean there's something horribly wrong with me, does it?
Have you noticed a change in your appetite lately?

Well, um... no, not really. I think I'm eating about the same as I always do. I mean, I might not have the biggest appetite right now, but I'm definitely still eating. 

I make sure to have my meals because I need the energy for work, you know? My clients rely on me, so I can't just skip eating. I guess maybe I'm not craving my favorite foods as much, but I'm still getting enough nutrition and everything. That's the important part, right? As long as I'm keeping my strength up, a little change in appetite isn't anything to worry about, is it? I just want to make sure I'm doing all the right things to take care of myself.
Have you been feeling worthless or blaming yourself a lot lately?

Oh, well, I wouldn't say I feel *worthless*, exactly. I mean, I know I do good work with my clients, and I try to be a good person... I really don't want to sound like I'm just sitting around throwing a pity party for myself. 

But, um... I guess... well, since my tío passed, I have been having a hard time with... just thinking about things I could have done better. Like, I keep replaying it all in my head, you know? Thinking I really should have called him more often, or... or made the time to visit him sooner before things got bad. And sometimes I just end up feeling like... like I really let him down. Like I failed him as family. 

But I know everyone has regrets when someone passes away, right? It's normal to wish you had done more, isn't it? I'm trying not to be too hard on myself, because I know he wouldn't want me to feel guilty. I just want to make sure I'm processing it the right way... does that make sense?
Since your uncle died, has this been making it hard for you to function in your day-to-day life?

Well, um... I wouldn't say it's making it *hard* to function, exactly. I mean, I'm still going to work every day, still taking care of my clients. I would never just stop doing my job, you know? They really need me.

But, I guess... well, I have been leaning on people a little bit more than usual. Just to be safe. Like at work, I've asked some of my coworkers to just double-check my client documentation for me. Not because I can't do it, but just... just to make sure I haven't missed any small details while my head's a little foggy from the grief. And at home, my wife has been so great, she's taken over paying some of the bills and doing the scheduling for a bit. Just because I haven't been quite as reliable with keeping track of all those little things right now. 

But I'm still doing the important stuff, you know? It's okay to ask for a little help when you're going through a tough time, right? I just want to make sure I'm doing everything right so nobody else is affected by what I'm going through. That's the responsible thing to do, isn't it?
Since your uncle died, have you been pulling away from spending time with other people?

Oh, no, definitely not. Um... I know sometimes people isolate themselves when they're grieving, but I really try not to do that. It wouldn't be fair to my wife or my friends to just shut them out, you know? 

I'm still talking to my coworkers every day, and I make sure to spend time with my family in the evenings. Like I said, I've actually been leaning on them a little bit more lately, so I'm definitely not hiding away or anything. I think it's really important to stay connected to your support system when things are tough. That's the healthiest way to handle it, right? I just want to make sure I'm dealing with everything the right way so I don't become a burden to anyone.
Since your uncle died, have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I'm completely drained or anything like that. I still get up and go to work, and I try my best to keep up with everything. I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining or just being lazy. 

But, I guess... well, I have noticed that even on days when I don't do a whole lot, my body just feels... kind of worn out. Like, even simple things at work, like helping one of my clients with a shower, or just bringing the groceries in at home... it just seems to take a lot more out of me than it usually does. 

I know grief can take a physical toll on a person, right? It's pretty normal to feel a little more tired when you're going through something emotional, isn't it? I'm just trying to push through it and make sure I'm still doing what I need to do. I hope that makes sense.
If your uncle had not died, do you think you would still be feeling this sad and foggy right now?

Oh, um... no, I really don't think so. Before he passed, I was doing just fine. I was keeping up with all my clients and everything at home was perfectly normal. I didn't feel like this at all. 

It's really just been since we lost him. I mean, losing a family member is a big shock, right? I'm pretty sure anyone would feel a little sad and out of sorts after something like that. It's just a normal reaction to grief, don't you think? I really believe I'd be my usual self right now if he were still here. I just need a little time to process it all, that's all.
Since your uncle died, have you been feeling especially nervous or on edge?

Um... no, I don't think so. I haven't really been feeling nervous or, you know, jittery at all. 

I mean, obviously it's been a tough time, but I'm not walking around on edge or snapping at anyone or anything like that. I try really hard to stay calm, especially for my clients at work. They rely on me to be steady, you know? So I just make sure to keep a level head. 

I hope that's okay—I know everyone handles loss differently, but for me, anxiety hasn't really been an issue. It's really just the sadness and feeling a bit worn out, like we talked about. That's still a pretty normal way to grieve, isn't it?
Since your uncle died, have you been feeling hopeless?

Well, um... hopeless is a pretty strong word, isn't it? I wouldn't say I feel hopeless. I mean, I still get up every day and do my job, and I know things will eventually get better. I'm not giving up or anything like that. 

I guess... sometimes I have moments where it feels like the sadness is going to last a long time, but that's just because I miss him so much. It's not like I don't see a future or think everything is ruined. I just take it one day at a time, you know? That's the right way to handle it, isn't it? Just keeping a positive outlook as best I can?
Since your uncle died, have you been enjoying your usual activities less than you normally do?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I'm still doing all the things I usually do. I still like watching my shows in the evening and, you know, keeping up with my normal routine. 

Obviously, I'm grieving, so maybe I'm a little quieter than usual, but I haven't lost interest in my life or anything. I still get enjoyment out of my hobbies. I think it's really important to keep doing the things you love when you're going through a tough time, don't you? It helps keep you grounded. So, yeah, I'm still enjoying things just fine. That's a good sign, right?
In the past two weeks, have you felt sad or down most of the day nearly every day?

Well... I mean, I guess it depends on what you mean by most of the day. I definitely don't want to sound like I'm just sitting around crying all the time, because I'm not. I still go to work and take care of my clients, and I can talk to them and be cheerful when I need to be. 

But... lately, I guess I do wake up with this kind of heavy, empty feeling in my chest. It's like... I can get through my shift just fine, but underneath it all, I just feel kind of sad and flat. It's not like I'm letting it ruin my day or affect my work, though. I still push through. That's pretty normal when you've lost someone, right? Just feeling a little heavy for a while?
